title: Relative nonspecial Abel chart with prescribed fibre divisor
statement: Let $S$ be locally Noetherian [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], and let $f:X\to S$ be flat, finitely presented and projective in the projective-bundle sense, with nonempty geometrically connected reduced nodal fibres [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism, def-trf-nodal-geometric-fibres]. Suppose the Picard fppf sheaf $P=\operatorname{Pic}_{X/S}$ is represented by an algebraic space [sk-def-picard-pic, def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $A\subseteq P$ be an open subgroup [def-a1-space-open-subspace]. Fix $s\in S$, a separable closure $k_s$ of $\kappa(s)$, and an effective divisor $E_s$ consisting of $g=\dim_{k_s}H^1(X_{k_s},\mathcal O)$ distinct smooth $k_s$-points with $H^1(X_{k_s},\mathcal O(E_s))=0$ and $H^0(X_{k_s},\mathcal O(E_s))=k_s$ [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle, def-sc-sheaf-cohomology-functor]. There is an etale neighbourhood $S'\to S$ of this geometric point and a relative effective Cartier divisor $E\subset X_{S'}$ extending $E_s$ [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-pc-relative-effective-cartier]. There is a quasi-compact open subspace $V\subseteq A_{S'}$ containing the entire identity section, and a scheme $W$, open in the degree-$g$ relative divisor scheme of the smooth locus of $X_{S'}/S'$, with an isomorphism $W\simeq V$. On test schemes this map sends a divisor $F$ to $[\mathcal O(F-E)]$. Its inverse sends a class $[L]$ to the zero divisor of the evaluation $f_T^*f_{T,*}(L(E))\to L(E)$, on the locus where $f_{T,*}(L(E))$ is invertible with arbitrary base change and this evaluation cuts out a relative divisor in the smooth locus. The neighbourhood may be shrunk to be affine Noetherian. The assertions include $g=0$.

source.place: Lemma 4.5 and its proof, printed p.143: extension of the smooth fibre divisor, cohomology-and-base-change rank-one locus, and inverse evaluation-divisor construction. Quasi-compactness follows by taking an affine Noetherian neighbourhood and a quasi-compact open around the identity inside the finite-type divisor chart. Primary Numdam PDF read online; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Restrict first to an affine Noetherian neighbourhood $S_0$ of $s$. By [lem-trf-projective-bundle-proper] $f$ is proper. The structure line on $S_0$ is ample by [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]: its section $1$ has nonvanishing open $S_0$. Thus [lem-trf-projective-bundle-to-h-projective] gives a closed embedding into a finite projective space over $S_0$. Let $U$ be the relative smooth locus. [lem-sfb-flat-space-smooth-locus] identifies its fibres and all its base changes with the fibre smooth loci. Its relative dimension is one, since the geometric fibres are nodal curves. Each of the finitely many points of $E_s$ has image $x_i\in U_s$ closed in this fibre, with finite separable residue field over $\kappa(s)$: its residue field embeds in the algebraic separable extension $k_s$, and is finitely generated over $\kappa(s)$. Apply [lem-sbc-smooth-separable-point-etale-slice] to $U\to S_0$ at each $x_i$. The resulting affine etale base maps have lifts to $U$. Their residue fields embed in $k_s$ compatibly with the prescribed $k_s$-points, since they are finite separable extensions. Take their fibre product, pointed by these lifts. The base-change and composition assertions of [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus] make this an etale neighbourhood with sections $\sigma_i$ lifting all points of $E_s$. For $g=0$ take $S_0$ itself and no sections.

source.place: Deligne 4.5, first paragraph: extend the smooth fibre divisor; Stacks 057G, 01WC and smooth-locus calculus

proof.text: The sections are closed in $X$ because $f$ is separated: a section is the pullback of the diagonal, and [def-weil-proper-morphism] and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] give closedness. For the same reason the equalizer of each pair $\sigma_i,\sigma_j$ is closed in the new base. Remove the finitely many equalizers, which miss the prescribed point, and take an affine open neighbourhood there. The sections are now disjoint. Each image is Cartier in $U$ by [lem-trf-smooth-curve-section-cartier]. Their disjoint union $E$ is Cartier in $X$: near its support this is the assertion for the single section present; off the support its ideal is the unit ideal. It is finite locally free of rank $g$ over the base, since it is the disjoint union of $g$ copies of that base, and hence is relative effective Cartier. It restricts to the specified $E_s$. The base can be kept affine Noetherian: the etale affine slices over an affine Noetherian base are finite type, and so are their finite affine fibre products; use [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], then [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian] for the open restrictions. Call the resulting neighbourhood $S_1$. For $g=0$, $E=\varnothing$, whose ideal is $\mathcal O_X$.

source.place: Deligne 4.5, extension of D; Stacks 067R, affine Noetherian restriction

proof.text: For a line module $L$ on $X_T$ with $T\to S_1$, put $B=L\otimes\mathcal O(E_T)$. The divisor and its line module commute with arbitrary base change by [lem-pc-recd-pullback]. The line $B$ is finitely presented and flat over $T$: on a trivializing open its stalk is the flat stalk of $\mathcal O_{X_T}$. Therefore [lem-sfb-proper-flat-space-derived-base-change], applied to this scheme as an algebraic space, makes $K_T(B)$ perfect and universally compatible with derived base change, and its degree-zero cohomology $\epsilon_{T,*}f_{\mathrm{et},*}B_{\mathrm{et}}$ is the usual direct image $p_*B$, since the associated etale sheaf has the sections of $B$ over Zariski opens. Apply [lem-pc-perfect-locus] with degree $0$ and rank $1$. It gives a base-change-compatible open of $T$ on which $K_T(B)=N[0]$ for an invertible $N=p_*B$. On this open, for every further base change $h$, the derived comparison has source $h^*N[0]$ because $N$ is locally free. Taking degree zero gives exactly $h^*p_*B\simeq p'_*B'$. Thus this open has the arbitrary ordinary base-change property required for the evaluation map.

source.place: Deligne 4.5, rank-one cohomology-and-base-change locus; Stacks 0CTM and 0BDK

proof.text: On the rank-one open form the evaluation $p^*N\to B$. Apply [lem-sfb-section-finite-cartier-open-locus] to this morphism, the smooth open $U_T$ and $d=g$. This gives a further open where its zero scheme $F$ is a relative effective Cartier divisor in $U_T$, finite locally free of rank $g$. These conditions descend to Picard classes. Indeed if $L$ is replaced by $L\otimes p^*Q$ for a line $Q$ on $T$, then, on an open trivializing $Q$, direct image and evaluation are the previous ones tensored by that trivial line. The transition units of $Q$ give $N'=N\otimes Q$; the coefficient defining the zero ideal is unchanged when both source and target are tensored. Hence the two opens and the divisor agree. For two local representatives of the same Picard sheaf section this comparison applies after a further fppf cover by the sheafification description [sk-def-picard-pic]. It follows that these opens agree on overlaps of local representatives. Take the scheme coproduct of a small family of fppf-local bundle presentations, using [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Apply [lem-trf-fppf-local-open-subfunctor-descent] to the resulting presentation and its invariant open. This constructs an open subspace $V_1\subseteq A_{S_1}$, and the preceding rule constructs its evaluation divisor on every test scheme. The divisor is compatible with pullback by [lem-pc-zero-scheme-pullback] and the degree-zero comparison of Step 3; The divisor functor is represented by the scheme of [lem-sfb-projective-smooth-divisor-parameter], hence is an fppf sheaf by [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]; the local divisors therefore descend uniquely.

source.place: Deligne 4.5, second open locus and independence of the representative; Stacks 062Y and 02WU

proof.text: The identity over the prescribed point belongs to $V_1$. For $L=\mathcal O$, the hypotheses give $h^0(\mathcal O(E_s))=1$ and $h^1(\mathcal O(E_s))=0$. All cohomology above degree one vanishes by [lem-sfb-proper-space-curve-qcoh-bound]; there is no negative cohomology of a sheaf direct image. By the base-change isomorphism of Step 3 the derived fibre of $K(\mathcal O(E))$ at the geometric point is etale cohomology of $\mathcal O(E_s)$ on $X_{k_s}$, which [lem-sc-etale-zariski-qcoh-comparison] identifies with the Zariski cohomology of the hypotheses. Step 3 therefore puts this point in the rank-one open. The canonical section $1_{E_s}$ has zero scheme $E_s$ by [lem-sc-canonical-section-zero-scheme]. It is nonzero, since a Cartier divisor cannot equal a nonempty curve; hence it spans the one-dimensional space of sections. Evaluation thus has precisely zero scheme $E_s$, so Step 4 applies there. Pull back the open $V_1$ along the identity section $S_1\to A_{S_1}$, and replace $S_1$ by an affine open neighbourhood of the specified point inside this inverse image. Its restricted identity section lies entirely in $V_1$. Denote this affine Noetherian etale neighbourhood by $S'$ and the restricted open by $V$.

source.place: Deligne 4.5: the constructed open contains the zero section, after shrinking the base

proof.text: The projective embedding from Step 1 persists on $S'$. The geometric fibres have pure dimension one: they are connected of dimension one, and a zero-dimensional irreducible component of a Noetherian connected scheme lying in no other component would be an open and closed point. Apply [lem-sfb-projective-smooth-divisor-parameter] with $d=g$ to obtain the finite-type divisor scheme $H_g$. Its universal divisor $F_{\rm univ}$ is relative Cartier and its line commutes with pullback. By [sk-def-picard-pic] it gives the morphism $\alpha:H_g\to P_{S'}$, $F\mapsto[\mathcal O(F-E)]$. Let $W=\alpha^{-1}(V)$, an open subscheme of $H_g$. Step 4 gives a natural map $\beta:V\to H_g$ by evaluation divisors. For a local representative $L$ with $B=L(E)$ and $N=p_*B$, [lem-pc-zero-scheme-divisor-iso] applied to $p^*N\to B$ gives $B\simeq\mathcal O(F)\otimes p^*N$. Consequently $[\mathcal O(F-E)]=[L]$ in the Picard sheaf. These equalities hold fppf-locally for every section and hence hold in that sheaf; thus $\alpha\beta=\mathrm{id}_V$. In particular $\beta$ factors through $W$.

source.place: Deligne 4.5, final identification with an open divisor scheme; Stacks 01X0

proof.text: Conversely take $F\in W(T)$ and represent $\alpha(F)$ by $L=\mathcal O(F-E)$. Then $B=\mathcal O(F)$ and the rank-one condition gives the line $N=p_*\mathcal O(F)$ with arbitrary base change. The canonical section $1_F$ of [lem-sc-canonical-section-zero-scheme] induces $c:\mathcal O_T\to N$. On every residue-field fibre it is nonzero: [lem-pc-recd-pullback] makes $F_t$ Cartier on the nonempty fibre, and the zero scheme of the canonical section is exactly $F_t$. It cannot be the entire fibre. Since $H^0(\mathcal O(F_t))$ has dimension one, $c_t$ is an isomorphism. Locally $c$ is multiplication by an element of a local ring; nonzero residue means that element is a unit. Thus $c$ is an isomorphism. With this generator, evaluation is the canonical section and has zero scheme $F$. This proves $\beta\alpha=\mathrm{id}_W$, naturally for arbitrary $T$. Hence $W\simeq V$ and the two maps have precisely the formulas asserted.

source.place: Deligne 4.5, verification of the inverse on test schemes; canonical Cartier section

proof.text: The scheme $H_g$ is finite type over the Noetherian $S'$, so is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Its open $W$ is Noetherian and quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. The isomorphism makes $V$ quasi-compact as well. When $g=0$ the construction uses the empty divisor and $H_0=S'$. At the prescribed point its canonical section is $1$ with empty zero scheme; Steps 3--7 apply without a section-lifting choice or a positive-degree assumption. Thus this case is included.

source.place: Quasi-compact refinement of Deligne 4.5 over an affine Noetherian neighbourhood; degree zero case
